adversarial_refutations.argument:
Row cor:flat-carriers (SM.flat_carriers / FlatCarriersData). I tried to build a flat-wall germ (n+1 >= 4, flat at j, sides P(+-t), centre C = P(0), deletion D = P(0)\j) and a support S on which the geo* construction departs from the printed one, along every axis named in the task. None produced a discrepancy; each attack closes on a definitional identity I checked in the accepted modules.

1. Mark ordering at the non-generic centre. geoMarkList sorts Mark C = ZMod(n+1) ⊕ Visit C by geoMarkKey = traversalKey(geoMarkPosition) = i.val + t (Traversal.lean:17), vertex at (i,0), visit at (v.2.val, crossingParameter) (GeometricVisits.lean:12). Under flatCentreCG = flat_crossingGeometry, IsCrossing (remote closed segments meet, Crossings.lean:12) coincides with the printed "transverse intersection of relative interiors" because CrossingGeometry.2 forces any common point of remote segments to be interior with det != 0, so crossingPoint (Classical.choose of a common point) is the unique crossing point and the parameter is strictly interior and injective (geoMarkPosition_injective). Traversal order at the centre is therefore mu_{j-1} < visits on E_{j-1} < mu_j < visits on E_j < mu_{j+1}, exactly the sides' order (lem:flat-sides (ii) "constant order on every edge") and, after erasing mu_j, the deletion's order on the fused edge (FlatFusionData: fusionParameter r j k t = r*t on E_{j-1}, r+(1-r)*t on E_j, order preserving). Attempted degenerate visits (a visit at mu_j, or E_{j-1} meeting E_{j+1}) require a second collinear triple, excluded by hz = {turnSupport j} (PointZeroTriple = any collinear triple) together with StrictBetween; so no configuration gives an extra or misplaced mark at the centre.

2. The zero-turn vertex mu_j. Sum.inl j is a vertex mark, hence IsTrueCorner (CarrierTrueCorners.lean:44), hence a corner of geoCornerPolygon at the centre; its turn = chi(prev, mu_j, next) = sgn det(alpha*d_{j-1}, beta*d_j) = 0 with alpha,beta>0 (all skipped marks between corners lie on the same edge line), and every other centre corner turn is nonzero (vertex corners: chi(i-1,i,i+1) != 0 for i != j by hz; selected-visit corners: det(d_e,d_f) != 0). This is exactly turns_nonzero.1 (turn = 0 <-> corner = inl j), no_antiparallel is satisfied (parallel positive multiples), and rotationNumber = sum principalTurn/(2pi) with principalTurn = arg(conj(u)*v) = 0 at that corner, so the round-4 centre-copy rotation clause is well posed. Matches "except for that one central zero turn". On D, mu_j is not a mark and the fused direction is edge D (-1) = D 0 - D (-1) = P(j+1) - P(j-1) = w (deleteVertex_zero/_last, deletionIndex j i = i.val + j + 1), as used in central_vs_deletion_through_mu_j.5.

3. delMark / fusionMark. Vertex maps deletionIndex j / fusionIndex j are mutually inverse away from j (fusionIndex_deletionIndex, deletionIndex_exhaust); visit maps are fusionVisitEquiv^{-1} / fusionVisitEquiv = sigmaCongr(fusionCrossingEquiv, edge -> fusionIndex j) (FusionVisits.lean:39), which preserves crossing points and pairing (FlatFusionData). I checked the skip-mu_j successor law correspond_deletion.1 case by case (E_{j-1} with visits; E_{j-1} without visits so rho^C(mu_{j-1}) = mu_j and the law routes to rho(mu_j); a selected visit whose twin is the last mark on E_{j-1}): each time rho_S^D(b) = delMark(...) as written. deletionCopyThroughJ = owner_D(delMark(rho_S^C(inl j))) is well named since rho(inl j) is the first mark on E_j or mu_{j+1}, never inl j. The junk value delMark(inl j) is excluded by every guard (a != inl j, fusionMark_ne_deleted).

4. Right/left naming. Printed sm-1:743-744: right side = tau_j = -1, left = +1. Lean turn P i = chi P (i-1) i (i+1) = sgn det(d_{i-1}, d_i) (Chirotope.lean:13), +1 = counterclockwise = left; IsRightSide = turn (sideTuple b t) j = -1. extra_corner gives -1 on the right side: the side corner polygon's turn at mu_j(t) is sgn det(alpha*d_{j-1}(t), beta*d_j(t)) = tau_j(t). cornerSelector (1 if all turns -1, (-1)^k if all +1, else 0) with k = geoCornerCount (corners of that side's carrier, including mu_j) reproduces the sm-4:205 table (1,0,1) and (0,(-1)^{k+1},(-1)^k), so selector_identity is the printed W_right - W_left = W_del.

5. Reconnection and carriers. geoSmoothingSuccessor = (selectedMarkPerm S).trans (geoMarkSuccessor) = rho o swap with the same selectedMarkPerm = sumCongr refl selectedVisitTwinPerm as the accepted SmoothingData and SelectedVisitsConventionData; the successor of visit a of a selected crossing is rho(twin a) = "incoming arc at a reconnected to the outgoing arc at b", and a stays in its own rho_S cycle, which is the incoming-visit convention (the incoming segment [pt(rho^-1 a), pt a] is the rho_S step from swap(rho^-1 a) to a). GeoComponent = cycles of rho_S; geoComponentMarkList = traversal-order filter (identical to accepted componentMarkList); for GeoIndependent S (GeometricInterlaces = cyclic alternation of the geometric positions) the noncrossing-chord faces are traversed in circular order, so traced_successor holds; corner list/polygon = accepted ccpCornerList/ccpCornerPolygon word for word, and on generic sides geoComponentEquivGeneric ties them to the accepted Component. geometricGaussWord is a Cycle, so the deletion clause (cut at mu_{j+1} vs mu_0) is compared cyclically; no false list equation.

Non-blocking reading choices (not refutations): both sides are taken at the same |t| via sideTuple b t (the printed sides are chambers, so content is equivalent); centre_turn_signs, identify_*_marks, same_signs for all visits and unique_through_mu_j on the sides are STRONGER than the printed clauses, as flagged in PLAN_FINAL §3; "contains mu_j" is read as the plane point, and the Lean correctly makes no deletion claim although D's fused edge passes through the point mu_j. I found no concrete germ and support on which marks, successor, reconnection, carriers, corner polygon or turns differ from the printed construction, so the row is not refuted.
